subject: Eval gating & commit runway — GPU tranche schedule and MAP
messages:
From: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@orion-analytics.com>

Cc: procurement@orion-analytics.com
Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP / Eval timeline and GPU sizing questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. We're ready to formalize a Mutual Action Plan so our internal teams (platform, procurement, security) can align on milestones toward a May pilot target. A few asks from our side to include in the MAP:

- Clear lead times for Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) procurement and realistic ramp cadence per tranche.
- Recommended GPU pool sizing for a 2-week pilot vs initial production tranche (RPS and token assumptions are below).
- Gating criteria for progressing from pilot -> canary -> full production.
- Any options for short-term burst capacity if our traffic spikes during evaluation.

Attached is a short requirements spreadsheet (requirements_summary.xlsx) — it contains sample traffic profiles, token lengths, and security checklist items.

Can you draft a MAP with those specifics and send it back by Monday? Also, if you can call out expected SLA exceptions / onboarding tasks that would speed procurement and on-prem readiness, that would help my legal and infra teams.

Best,
Sarah

Orion Analytics

Date: 2027-02-28T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP / Eval timeline and GPU sizing questions

Sarah — thanks, attached is a first draft MAP (MAP_Orion_v1.0.xlsx). Key excerpts below to make the major decisions explicit in thread: 

1) High-level MAP milestones (proposed)
- Week 0: Kickoff + SOW signatures + initial access (credentials + test dataset)
- Weeks 1-2: Pilot (functional verification, smoke perf) — Pilot pool: 2 x A100-80GB (q8 quantized)
- Weeks 3-5: Performance evaluation (load tests, latency P95, token throughput) — target: p95 < 120ms on tail-optimized routings, sustained 250k tokens/sec aggregate on pilot pool
- Weeks 6-8: Security & compliance (SOC2 docs, VPC peering, KMS proof points)
- Weeks 9-12: Procurement & capacity tranche 1 delivery (see lead times below)

2) Procurement lead-time & recommended runway
- Redwood Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity): typical lead time for tranche provisioning: 6-10 weeks from signed PO to reserved pool active.
- Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem options): customer-managed on-prem racks or air-gapped setups: 12-20 weeks depending on rack procurement and shipping windows.
- Recommendation: structure MAP to commit to an initial small tranche (tranche A) to meet near-term needs and a scheduled tranche B for month+3 to absorb growth. This staggers procurement risk and lets us tune kernel/quantization on live traffic.

3) GPU pool sizing (three scenarios)
- Conservative (pilot -> steady): Pilot 2xA100-80GB (q8) -> Prod Tranche A: 6xA100 (expected 400k tokens/sec, budget-conscious)
- Expected (recommended): Pilot 2xA100 -> Prod Tranche A: 4xH100 + 4xA100 equivalent (750k tokens/sec, target p95 110ms)
- Aggressive (fast growth): Prod Tranche A: 12xH100 equivalent (1.6M tokens/sec, p95 target 90-100ms)

Note: these numbers reflect our runtime optimizations (KV caching, prefix caching, and continuous batching). We'll provide per-model kernel guidance once you lock the model version.

4) Gating criteria to move from Pilot -> Canary -> Prod
- Functional: all test cases pass and generation correctness within agreed eval set (pass rate >= 95%)
- Performance: sustained throughput target for the pilot pool for 48 hours; p95 latency target met in 95% of test windows
- Cost signal: marginal cost per 1M tokens below the agreed budget threshold (see MAP sheet)
- Security: SOC2 evidence & network peering validated

5) Short-term burst & canary options
- We can provide limited burst capacity from hosted spare pool for 2x baseline for up to 72 hours while your procurement completes; needs a short-term addendum in MAP for billing and failback rules.

6) On-prem notes
- On-prem introduces two wildcards: rack lead time and customs/import delays. Recommend starting private planning in parallel with Dedicated commit if time-to-production matters.

Next steps: 1) review MAP_Orion_v1.0.xlsx, 2) confirm which sizing scenario you want to gate on, 3) confirm procurement PO timeline and internal approvers. I propose a joint MAP sync on Thu Mar 4 10:00 PT to sign off.

Logan
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Orion MAP — pricing, tranche ask, and operational tasks

Team — quick internal sync notes after sending the draft to Orion: 

- Deal context: Orion's pilot target is May; they asked for May pilot runway and a May->June production slice. Deal id ORION-2027-052.
- Pricing levers: Ben, can you prepare commit tiers for 3 tranche sizes (Conservative/Expected/Aggressive) with 12/24 month options and an early-burst credit line?
- Onboarding/SLA exceptions: Marissa, we should pre-author the 48h burst allowance and an onboarding ramp clause (we may need a 10% extra cache at onboarding to keep p95 targets).
- Capacity check: Karthik, confirm availability for 4xH100 + 4xA100 equivalent for tranche A in our US pool; also confirm if HIPAA/PCI certs add to lead time for Private targets.
- Doc flow: I will include the MAP and PO template in the DocuSign link when Orion confirms; we should be ready with a PO template that labels tranche dates and shipment windows explicitly.

Please flag anything I missed. Aim to have Ben's pricing table and Karthik's availability by EOD Mar 2 so we can present at the Mar 4 sync.

Thanks,
Logan

Logan — thanks for the thorough MAP. We reviewed MAP_Orion_v1.0 with engineering and procurement this morning. A few quick confirmations:

- We accept the 48h short-term burst clause — please include billing rules in the final MAP.

Procurement will sign the MAP doc via the DocuSign link once Ben confirms price bands. Attaching a signed stub to speed legal review (signed_map_stub.pdf).

Sarah
